- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 90+), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture the “rebound” or “mean reversion” after peaks.
- Model underestimates when true price drops below 80, especially in the final 5–10 days of the forecast window.
- Model exhibits lag: true price often dips below forecast before the model adjusts — suggests model reacts too slowly to downward momentum.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility: if history includes a spike, forecast often overcorrects downward, then fails to recover.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted: model doesn’t sufficiently anticipate prices returning to prior averages after short-term deviations.
- Forecast bias is downward in the final 10–15 days — model systematically underestimates prices near the end of the 30-day window.
